sectors.name: Government Contracting
sectors.sourceNote: sbLiftOff, 'Knowing Your Company's Value is a Key to Growth – And Exit!' (Oct 2022, EBITDA). Advisor-stated ranges for small set-aside government contractors: 3–5× set-aside designations with no full-and-open work, 5–7× some full-and-open, 5–9×+ all full-and-open. Table uses 3.0–7.0×; override upward for mostly full-and-open firms. Not a licensed transaction database; figures taken from search-result snippets and not yet confirmed against the live page.
sectors.methodNote: Low = bottom of the set-aside-only tier (3×). High = top of the middle tier (7×), chosen over the 9×+ full-and-open ceiling as the conservative default for $1M–$5M EBITDA firms. Set-aside dependence is the dominant value driver here and is not captured by the scorecard: SBA recertification rules effective 2026-01-17 can make an acquired small business ineligible for set-aside option years. Use the assessment override with a note for set-aside-heavy clients. Larger-deal sources (Capstone Partners 2026 A&D avg 9.5–11.4× EV/EBITDA; Chesapeake Corporate Advisors Q1 2026 public Government Services 11.5×) describe $5M+ EBITDA or public companies and were rejected for this size band.
